scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance is influenced by the Natha Pantha tradition.
It is a long-standing practice of the Arebhahse community in Sullia, performed during the Suggi month.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed during the full moon of the Suggi month.
It is a religious ritual involving prayers to Kadri Manjunatha and local spirits, serving as a form of mythological mimicry.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performers move from house to house, dancing around a central lamp.
The Sanyasi character roams the courtyard independently, interacting with the public using provocative language.
The group chants 'Ḍimbisāle' while moving between locations.
on_screen: Formation: Performers move from house to house, dancing around a central lamp in the courtyard.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music includes singing and the use of a conch and drum, particularly by the Dasayya character.
The primary vocal element is the chanting of 'Ḍimbisāle' and specific ritual songs.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes vary by character: the Sanyasi wears dried camouflage leaves and a wooden phallus; the Dasayya wears a white dhoti, red shawl, and Mundasu; the Bhatru wears a sacred thread and sandalwood paste; the Koraga is covered in dark paint; the Byari wears a white banyan and traditional hat.
